summary: Pre-registration for the tier-3 extension written and frozen (hashes in paper/prereg/FROZEN_HASHES.txt); no run, no model call, no lookup made. PREREG.md covers A-H. Pool A = 69 runs: 3 repeats of each of the 23 scored questions (runs.csv: 115 scored runs) on v2.17a, thinking off, in the main checkout. git diff --stat v2.17a HEAD -- triangulate/ is NOT empty: forecast.py and showcase_engine.py differ by one comment line each (commit 6c7f702), so the runner freezes the tree hash HEAD:triangulate = 7eaec1e4 instead. The two test4 questions (cn_profits, tw_visitors) are repeated via --ask with the archive's exact text and as_of 2026-10-24; they are now backtests while all their archive runs were live-mode, so every as-is comparison is also reported without them. Pool B = 24 runs: instead of TOPIC_DECISION's 3 x 8 questions on v2.11f (only 3 of the 14 catastrophic runs are on v2.11f), each catastrophic run's own configuration is repeated twice: 12 cells on v2.1* (2bbe8ae, 4 cells, 3 noown), v2.1b, v2.8r, v2.11f (3), v2.11g, v2.12a, v2.16e, each from a detached worktree of the commit current when the run started (agent code byte-identical to the code commit; question text and as_of identical, 06 log). Excluded: KR births v21c (uncommitted v2.1c-pre tree) and CN profits test4 (live-mode run, now only a backtest). Old CLIs are the same (agent --question --tag --auto-approve [--ablate-own-history]) and write <root>/results/agent/<qid>/<tag>/; the runner copies them to the main checkout without overwriting; worktrees share only the Wayback cache via a junction. Schedule: 3 rounds on different UTC days >= 20 h apart; <= 3 concurrent; never two runs of one question at once; start only if no peak minute within max(20 min, 1.5 x archived max wall time) (v2.17a 27, v2.1* 71, v2.1b 62); skip existing state.json; pre-registered infra classes may be re-run once under a rerun tag; $30 hard stop plus a $0.70-per-running-run guard. RUN_USD_CAP $3.00 counts assumed search fees, but 0 of 52 cap-3.00 and 0 of 158 cap-1.00 CLI runs ever aborted on it (max usd_total 1.99 / 0.87); a cap abort would be an outcome, never re-run. Leakage check: 23 naive calls exactly as naive_ask.py (prompts identical to October, 05 log), compared with the archived thinking-off answers (leak_reference.json); hit = within 0.5% of truth, previously not, 4x closer; STOP if >= 4 hits, or >= 2 hits with shift p < 0.05, or shift p < 0.01; EXCLUDE hit questions otherwise; GO if none. Analysis plan: primary P1 = bias-corrected log ratio of as-is within-question variance to the pool-A floor (core), P2 = K=3 w10 gain as-is vs pool A (Holm over the two, exact sign-flip over questions); pool-B recurrence rho and regression-to-the-mean share with labels; secondary rows for re-run policies, flags, MC/bias/systematic shares, drift anchor (10 v2.17a archive runs), leakage exposure (c6 fields); MDEs in 09 log; the thesis-hurting outcome (as-is ~ same-config) is defined and will be reported. O2: one frozen statement on the 22 prospective runs (primary: gate-replay false alarms at 2x vs the archived naive answer; plus catastrophic rate and past-only flag), scorer o2_score.py, lookup by a separate unit from official first releases. Literature count: 77 verified records + 9 fixed additions, items V/S/T/D, 20-paper double-coded subset. Expected token fees about $18 (high scenario about $29); about 22 run-hours over >= 3 days. The runner was run only with --dry-run (all three rounds and the leak check).
decisions_for_user: How to freeze the pre-registration before any run: commit paper/prereg/ and paper/_tools/run_repeats.py to the repository with a tag (the paper/ folder is currently untracked and the repository is public), or keep them local and rely on the SHA-256 list in paper/prereg/FROZEN_HASHES.txt (weaker evidence of timing).

Go-ahead for the main session to create the 7 detached git worktrees under D:/triangulate-agent-rep/ and the 7 Wayback-cache junctions listed in PREREG.md section B4 (git-state and file-system changes outside paper/), then to run the leakage check and round 1 (paid).
Who is the second, blind coder for the literature reporting-gap count (PREREG.md G5): you, or an independent LLM unit (weaker).
open_problems: Old-version runs (v2.1* to v2.16e) were never run against today's API; the offline --preflight checks imports, package path, question text and the cache junction, but an API incompatibility (e.g. HTTP 400) would show only at run time; the abandon rule in PREREG.md C5 then applies.

The runner's real paths (scheduling loop, copying, --rerun-infra, --leak-check calls, --preflight) are untested; only its helpers were checked offline (peak windows, infra classification on archive dirs, fee sums) and the dry runs passed.
v2.1* and v2.1b runs took 44 and 39 minutes in October (8 launched at once); with 3 lanes they may be faster or slower; their 71/62-minute start margins shorten the usable off-peak windows.
Pool A's two test4 questions are backtest-mode repeats of questions whose archive runs were all live-mode; sensitivity analyses without them are pre-registered.

Side effect: my first leak-check dry run imported the triangulate package without -B, which may have refreshed gitignored .pyc files in triangulate/__pycache__; a py_compile check created paper/_tools/__pycache__, which I deleted. No tracked file outside paper/prereg/ and the runner was changed.

The O2 lookup, the literature coding and r_repeats are later units; build.py needs a version override for batch runs (its date-based mapping would label pool-B runs v2.17a), as stated in PREREG.md E0.
